welcomeContent: In 10 short steps you'll draw two letters, try them out, and see how to get your font. Each step waits for you.
clickFirstChar: Let's start by creating your first letter. Click the 'A' card.
splitViewIntro: This is the split view. You can **drag this divider** to resize the panels. The grid also serves as a **quick navigator** to jump between characters.
toolbarPenContent: This is the Pen tool. It is selected by default. You can use it to draw freehand shapes.
drawContent: Draw 'A' over the faint guide letter with the **pen**. Wrote it on paper? The **camera** button (under **More** on a phone) traces a photo of it. Click **Next** when you're done.
clickNextForA: Good start! Click the Next arrow to continue to the letter 'a'.
toolbarIntro: This is the **Toolbar**. It contains freehand tools, precise shape tools, and action buttons.
toolbarActionsIntro: Great! The toolbar also has actions like Select, Pan, Undo, and Copy. Let's take a quick tour.
toolSelect: The **Select Tool** lets you click, move, resize, and rotate your shapes.
toolPan: Use the **Pan Tool** to click and drag your view around the canvas without moving your shapes.
toolCalligraphy: The **Calligraphy Pen** creates strokes with variable thickness, like a broad-nib pen. You can change the nib angle by clicking the tool icon again.
toolEraser: The **Eraser Tool** splits a path where you drag over it. It's great for creating gaps.
toolSlice: The **Slice Tool** cuts through a shape with a straight line, splitting it into two separate paths.
actionUndo: Made a mistake? **Undo** reverses your last action.
actionRedo: Changed your mind? **Redo** brings it back.
actionCut: Select a shape and click **Cut** to remove it and place it on your clipboard.
actionCopy: **Copy** places the selected shape on your clipboard without removing it.
actionPaste: **Paste** inserts the shape from your clipboard onto the canvas.
actionGroup: If you have multiple shapes selected, **Group** them to treat them as a single object.
actionUngroup: Select a group and click **Ungroup** to separate them back into individual shapes.
selectLineTool: The toolbar has **Shape Tools** for precise forms like lines, curves, and circles. Select the **Line Tool** now, then click 'Next'.
drawT: Use the Line Tool to construct the letter 'T' with two straight lines.
explainBearings: These two dashed upright lines set the **space on each side** of your letter.
dragLSB: Drag the small **handle** at the top or bottom of the **left** line to change the space on the left of your ‘T’. Then click Next.
dragRSB: Good. Now drag a handle of the **right** line. This space decides how close the next letter comes. When you’re done, click Next.
clickBackToDashboard: Click **Back** to see all your letters again.
clickAAgain: Select 'A' again to return to the editor.
openGrid: On smaller screens, click the floating **Grid button** to open the character list.
clickTest: Now try your letters. Click **Test** (the flask).
testPageInput: This is **Try your font**. Type here, for example **Aa aA**. Letters you haven't drawn yet show in grey boxes.
drawCharF: Draw the shape of 'F'. This is important because the next letter, 'E', uses this shape as a starting point.
clickNextForComposite: Let's see a powerful feature. Click Next to go to 'E'.
compositeExplanation: This is 'E'. It has been **pre-filled** with the shape of 'F'. You can now add strokes to finish the letter. Unlike linked glyphs, changes here are independent and won't affect the original 'F'.
drawComposite: Now, draw the bottom stroke to complete the 'E'. Notice how your new stroke combines with the pre-filled 'F' shape.
clickNextForLowerE: Let's draw a small 'e'. Click the **Next** arrow.
drawLowerE: Draw a simple 'e' on the canvas.
clickNextForLinked: Click Next again to see the magic of Linked Glyphs.
linkedExplanation: This is a combining mark. Notice it is already drawn! It is a **Linked Glyph** derived directly from the 'e' you just drew, scaled down automatically.
linkedStripNav: You can also navigate quickly between the Linked Glyph and its source components using this strip at the bottom.
transformLinked: Linked glyphs track the source shape, but their **position and size** are editable! Select the shape and try scaling or rotating it.
clickPrevForModification: Now, let's change the source. Click the **Previous Glyph** arrow to go back to 'e'.
modifyLowerE: Modify the 'e' significantly (e.g. add a circle around it).
clickNextToVerify: Go back to the linked glyph (Next).
verifyLink: See? the linked glyph updated automatically to match your changes!
explainBack: Now, click **Back** to return to the Character Grid so we can explore the final tools.
explainCreator: Open the **Creator Studio** to create artwork, stickers, and social media posts using your font.
explainCompare: Use **Compare** to view multiple characters side-by-side. Useful for checking consistency.
explainSettings: Adjust global font settings, metadata (like designer name), and view metrics here.
explainExport: When you're ready, click **Export Font**. The first time, it asks what your font should be called. Then it downloads the font file (.otf) and shows how to install and use it.
positioningNav: Finally, let's explore the powerful **Positioning** workspace. This is where you align marks, like accents or vowel signs, to base letters. Click the **Positioning** tab to continue.
positioningIntro: This is the Positioning Workspace. Here you'll align marks (like accents or vowel signs) to base letters and accept or adjust the app's automatic suggestions.
positioningViews: You can browse pairs in three ways: **By Rule** (groups similar pairs), **By Base** (shows all marks for a single base), or **By Mark** (shows a single mark on all bases).
positioningPreviewCard: This card shows a preview of the automatically positioned pair. The dashed border means it's an unconfirmed suggestion.
startPositioning: Click **Check Positioning** to review the pairs in this rule.
positioningAccept: To accept the automatic position for **Aͤ**, click the **Checkmark** button.
positioningEdit: Great! Now, let's fix one that might be incorrect. To make a manual adjustment, click on the **Eͤ** card to open the detailed editor.
positioningEditor: In this view, you can **drag the mark** into the perfect position. When you're satisfied with the alignment, click **Save** in the header. For now, just click 'Next' to finish the tour.
finish: You're ready to make your font! Positioning and Spacing are there when you've drawn your letters.
hintGridSelect: Welcome! Select a character card to start drawing your font.
hintEditorDraw: The **Pen Tool** is active. Click and drag on the canvas to draw your character shape.
hintRelatedPairsContent: This pair belongs to a **Smart Class**. Any position changes you make here will automatically sync to all **Related Pairs** shown in this strip.
hintOverrideContent: Need a unique position for this specific pair? Click this button to **Unlink**. This creates an **Override**, allowing you to move this mark independently without affecting the rest of the class.
hintCompositeContent: This glyph is constructed from components. It has been pre-filled for you. You can edit the paths, or use the **Refresh** button to update it if the source components change.
hintLinkedContent: This is a **Linked Glyph**. Its shape is automatically constructed from other characters (e.g. Base + Mark). It updates live when the source characters change.
hintUnlinkContent: To edit the shape manually, you must **Unlink** it first. This breaks the connection to the source components and converts it to a standard glyph.
hintRelinkContent: You have unlinked this glyph. It is now independent. If you want to revert to the automatic shape, click the **Relink** button here. Note: This will discard your manual edits.
hintPositionedContent: This is a **Positioned Pair**. It is dynamically generated by placing a Mark relative to a Base character. You can adjust the position coordinates here.
hintDetachContent: Need to edit the shape itself? Click **Detach** to convert this live pair into an **Independent Glyph**. You can then edit the shape manually.
hintAcceptPosition: Looks good? Click **Accept** will save this default calculated position as correct.
hintKernedContent: This is a **Kerned Pair**. It represents a specific spacing adjustment between two characters.
hintAcceptKerning: Looks good? Clicking **Accept** will save this default calculated spacing as correct.
hintKerningWorkspaceContent: This is where character pairs can be adjusted to have custom spacing.
hintPositioningWorkspaceContent: This is where characters are positioned to create perfect alignment.
clickNextForN: Let's see how accents are placed. Open 'n' from your letters.
clickNextForTilde: Now for the first mark. Click Next for the tilde (~).
drawTilde: Draw the tilde mark. It's a non-spacing mark, so it will automatically be positioned above letters.
clickNextForMacron: Let's add another mark to see how they sync. Click Next for the macron (¯).
clickNextForNTilde: Ready? Click Next to see 'ñ', which is automatically composed from 'n' and '~'.
positioningConcept: This is 'ñ'. The app automatically combined 'n' + '~' for you! This position is just a suggestion that you can change.
positioningStripIntro: This is the **Related Pairs** strip. It shows all characters in the same **Smart Class**. Changes you make to 'ñ' will automatically sync to 'n̄'.
positioningDrag: Now, try it! **Click and drag the tilde** to a new position. See how the 'n̄' thumbnail updates live? When you're done, click Next.
positioningStripNavToNBar: To verify the change, click on the **'n̄' thumbnail** in the strip to navigate directly to it.
smartClassExpl: Perfect! The position you set for the tilde on 'ñ' has been automatically applied to the macron on 'n̄'. This saves a lot of time!
positioningTryDragLocked: Now, try dragging the macron on `n̄` yourself.
positioningExplainLock: You'll notice it doesn't move. This is because it's part of a **Smart Class** and its position is synced to the `ñ` you edited earlier. To give this pair a unique position, you need to create an **Override**.
positioningClickUnlink: Click the **Synced** button in the control panel to unlink this pair from its class. **Then, click Next.**
positioningConfirmOverride: Excellent! This pair is now an **Override** and will no longer receive automatic updates from `ñ`. Notice the icon has changed.
positioningDragOverride: Now, **drag the macron again**. See? It moves freely. When you're ready, click Next.
positioningOverrideFinish: You've successfully created an exception. This powerful feature allows you to maintain consistency across a class while still handling special cases that require unique alignment.
threePillarsIntro: You've seen drawing. Two more screens finish a font: **Positioning** places accents and signs on letters, and **Spacing** sets the space between letters.
kerningNav: Last part: **Spacing**, the space between letters, overall and for pairs like 'Te' or 'AV'. Click the **Spacing** tab.
kerningIntroAndViews: Below are **Pair fixes**: pairs of letters that need to sit closer or further apart than usual. **Suggested pairs** are the ones to check, **Checked pairs** are done, and **All pairs** lets you fix any pair.
kerningManualEdit: Let's fix one manually. Click the **Te** card to open the editor.
kerningEditor: In the editor, **drag the right character** to adjust the space.
kerningClickBack: Great! The spacing is saved. Now click **Back** to return to the list.
kerningSpacedTab: The 'Te' pair you just adjusted is now in **Checked pairs**, with everything else that's done.
kerningAutoTools: **Space all automatically** spaces every pair in the list at once, straight into your font (Undo puts it back). **Find more pairs** looks through your letters for other pairs that need spacing and adds them here.
kerningAllPairsTab: To fix a pair that isn't suggested, use **All pairs**: choose letters from the side lists and adjust any pair.
finalCongratulations: **Well done!** You've seen the whole journey: drawing letters, placing accents, spacing and exporting. Your font is ready to grow.
compositeTools: Made a mistake? Use **Reset** to revert to the original template. If the source glyph (F) changes later, use **Refresh** to update this composite.
unlinkExpl: This glyph is locked to 'e'. To edit its shape manually (e.g., to make it wider), click the **Unlink** button.
relinkExpl: Now it is an independent shape. To restore the live link to 'e' and discard your manual changes, click **Relink**.
detachExpl: This pair is generated by math (Positioning). If you need to edit the *shape* of the mark specifically for this base (e.g., to squash it), click **Detach**. This converts it into a manual Composite glyph.
hintWhatIsKerningContent: Some pairs of letters (like 'A' and 'V') look too far apart or too close with normal spacing. Here you fix those pairs, and set the overall spacing of your font.
hintKerningViewsContent: **Suggested pairs** are the ones the app suggests checking. **Checked pairs** are done. **All pairs** lets you choose any pair yourself.
hintKerningToolsContent: **Space all automatically** measures the letters and spaces every pair in the list, straight into your font. **Find more pairs** looks through all your letters for pairs that touch or sit too far apart.
hintKerningAcceptContent: This spacing is in your font already. Don't like it? Click **Undo**. To adjust one pair, click it.
hintTestContent: You have drawn a character! Click here to test how it renders.
hintExportContent: Ready to use your font? Click here. The first time, it asks what your font should be called, then shows how to install it.
hintMetricsContent: The two upright lines set the **space on each side** of the letter. To change it, drag the small **handle** at the top or bottom of a line.
hintGridDottedContent: Cards with **dashed borders** are placeholders or auto-generated suggestions. Select them to review, draw, or accept them into your font.
coreExportAndFinish:
When your letters are ready, click **Export Font**. The first time, it asks what your font should be called; then it downloads the font and shows how to install it on a computer or a phone.

**That's the whole journey!** Other parts (drawing tools, letters made from other letters, accents, spacing) show a short tour the first time you open them. You can replay any of them from **Help → Tours**.
tourOpenAnyLetter: Open a letter, for example 'A', to see the drawing tools.
moreToolsTour: On a phone, the other tools are under **More**. Tap it to see them all, each with its name.
tracePhotoTour: Wrote the letter on paper? The **camera** button traces a photo of it and puts it on the letter, at the size of the guide letter.
fitViewTour: Zoomed in or out too far? **Show the whole letter** brings the normal view back.
spacingStripTour: At the top is **Overall spacing**: how close all letters sit, and how wide a word space is. The sample line shows the result in your own letters.
hintMobileMenuContent: Tap here to open the menu, then tap **Test** to try the letters you've drawn.
hintDrawerTestContent: Tap here to type with the letters you've drawn so far!
hintPosIntroContent: Here accents and signs are placed on letters. The buttons switch between seeing them **by rule** (groups of similar pairs), **by letter**, or **by sign**.
hintPosRulesContent: The app has already placed these accents and signs. **Check Positioning** opens them so you can check.
hintPosGridContent: Cards with a dashed border are suggestions. The **check mark** keeps the position as it is.
